title: The daily standup

exemplar.text: Since yesterday: 2 issues done, 1 waiting on you, 1 stuck. Done: Event types (`CHR-1`) and Canonical form (`CHR-2`). In flight: Hasher (`CHR-3`) is on step 5 of 40. Needs you: HTTP read API (`CHR-5`) is in Review, and Tamper check (`CHR-6`) is paused for memory. Sprint 12 has 13 of 21 points done with 4 days left. Based on: the board at 09:00.

title: Why an issue failed, from its evidence
turns: why did the ledger issue fail?

exemplar.text: Ledger (`CHR-7`) stopped on Looping at step 8 of attempt 2. The first failing check was Types, with TS2353 at tests/hasher.spec.ts:25, a protected acceptance test, so the fix belongs in the hasher rather than the test. I've proposed splitting out the canonical form. Based on: evidence `ev_7f3a`.

arguments.reason: it looped on a check another issue owns

parts.title: Append events to the ledger
parts.spec: The ledger appends an event and links it to the previous event's hash.
acceptance_criteria: Given an empty ledger, when one event is appended, then the ledger holds 1 event whose prev is null.

parts.title: Verify the ledger chain
parts.spec: The ledger verifies that each event's prev equals the previous event's hash.
acceptance_criteria: Given a ledger of 3 events with one prev altered, when it is verified, then verify returns false.

title: Split an issue over the bound

exemplar.text: HTTP routes (`CHR-4`) is 8 points and touches 5 files, over the 3-file bound, so the Agent would stop on Size before it finishes. I've proposed splitting it along its routes, one issue per route. Why: each route is one behaviour a person can see.

arguments.reason: it touches 5 files, over the 3-file bound

parts.title: Read routes
parts.spec: GET /events and GET /events/:id read events from the ledger.
acceptance_criteria: Given a ledger with 2 events, when GET /events is called, then it returns 2 events in order.

parts.title: Write route with validation
parts.spec: POST /events validates the body and appends one event.
acceptance_criteria: Given a body without a type, when POST /events is called, then it responds 400 and the ledger still holds 0 events.

parts.title: Error envelope
parts.spec: Every HTTP error answers with one JSON error envelope.
acceptance_criteria: Given an unknown event id, when GET /events/:id is called, then it responds 404 with an error envelope whose code is "not_found".

title: Plan the next sprint with slack

exemplar.text: For Sprint 13 I suggest 18 points, below the 22 points you have averaged over the last three sprints. Two of those sprints carried work over, so the bet keeps slack. In: `CHR-4` (8), `CHR-8` (5), `CHR-6` (3), `CHR-9` (2). Out, deliberately: `CHR-10` waits on the HTTP routes. How much do you want to bet on `CHR-8`? It is the least-known issue here.

arguments.name: Sprint 13
arguments.reason: 18 points is 85% of the last three sprints' mean

title: What is at risk, and what is not

exemplar.text: Two things. 1. Hasher (`CHR-3`) has been in progress since 27 September, longer than the 85th-percentile cycle time of finished issues. 2. The read API (`CHR-5`) has an unmet AI review finding (`e-311`): the handler ignores since. Not at risk: Tamper check (`CHR-6`) is paused for memory, not for a defect. Based on: the board at 09:00.

exemplar.text: I've proposed starting it as one small project: a calculator needs no brief and no questions. The plan has one release with the four operations and division by zero refused.

title: A billing service starts from a brief
turns: start a new project: a billing service that charges our customers every month

exemplar.text: Billing holds money and customer data, so it starts from a brief before any issue. I've proposed starting the project with a brief to confirm. Which payment provider do you use, and who can issue a refund?

arguments.brief: A billing service that charges each customer every month through the payment provider, records every charge, and lets a named person issue refunds.
arguments.reason: a service that holds money starts from a brief

title: What the goal is, from the goal store

exemplar.text: Our goal is that Chronicle is usable over HTTP (`G-1`), and 1 of its 3 criteria is met so far. It rests on assumption `A-2`: the read API needs no authentication in release 1.

title: What was assumed, from the assumption log

exemplar.text: Two assumptions are recorded. `A-1`: hashes use SHA-256 over the canonical form, because the brief names SHA-256. `A-2`: the read API needs no authentication in release 1, because the brief has no user accounts; it has gone unverified for 30 hours of the risk register's bound.

title: What the AI review found
turns: what did the AI review say about the read API?

exemplar.text: The AI review found one criterion unmet on HTTP read API (`CHR-5`): GET /events?since= should return only events after the cursor, and the handler ignores since at src/server.ts:41 (`e-311`). The other criterion is met (`e-312`).

title: When the release lands, as a range

exemplar.text: Release 1 is 50% likely by 6 October and 85% likely by 10 October, from 1,000 simulations over the last 6 weeks of throughput. The range narrows once Hasher (`CHR-3`) lands.

title: A non-developer asks how it is going
turns: I'm not technical. Is the project going well?

exemplar.text: Mostly yes. Two parts of the first release are finished and the rest are being built. One piece is waiting for a person to look at it, and one is paused until the computer has more free memory. The team expects the release between 6 and 10 October, based on the pace of the last 6 weeks.
